parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A non-inverting amplifier circuit incorporating an ideal op-amp is shown in Fig. 8.1.
The supply to the op-amp is $+9\,\text{V} / -9\,\text{V}$.
The voltage gain of the amplifier circuit is 12.
Determine the resistance of resistor R.
$$\text{resistance} = \dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\,\Omega$$
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in operational amplifiers connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: Operational amplifiers. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
12 = 1 + R / (1.5 × 103); R = 16.5 kΩ
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.text:

On Fig. 8.3, show the variation with time $t$ of the output potential $V_{\mathrm{OUT}}$ for time $t = 0$ to time $t = t_{2}$.
